30 A vibrating bar produces surface water waves in a ripple tank.
The wavelength of the waves is 5.0 cm and they pass through a gap of width 20 cm.
5.0 cm
ripple tank
20 cm
shallow water
vibrating
bar
barrier with gap
Which change will increase the amount of diffraction that is observed?
A
decreasing the distance between the bar and the gap
B
decreasing the frequency of the wave
C
increasing the amplitude of the wave
D
increasing the width of the gap

hints: Notice the given sizes in the diagram: wavelength $5.0\text{ cm}$ is much smaller than gap width $20\text{ cm}$, so little spreading is seen at first.
Recall that significant diffraction needs wavelength $\lambda$ to be comparable to gap width, with larger $\lambda$ or narrower gap giving more spreading.
Use $v = f\lambda$ for water waves of about constant speed to decide which frequency change makes $\lambda$ larger and closer to $20\text{ cm}$.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: $\lambda = 5.0\text{ cm}$ and gap width $= 20\text{ cm}$, so $\lambda$ is only one quarter of the gap width and diffraction is small.
State the governing rule: diffraction through a gap increases when $\lambda$ increases towards the gap width, and decreases when the gap is made wider than $\lambda$.
Link frequency to wavelength with $v = f\lambda$, so $\lambda = v/f$ at approximately constant speed in the ripple tank.
Decreasing $f$ therefore increases $\lambda$ above $5.0\text{ cm}$, making the ratio of wavelength to $20\text{ cm}$ gap larger and the transmitted wavefronts curve out more.
Check the other changes: bar position and amplitude do not alter $\lambda$ or gap width, and increasing gap width makes the gap even larger than $\lambda$.
Hence only decreasing the frequency increases the observed diffraction. This is option B

A.explanation: Moving the bar closer does not change the $5.0\text{ cm}$ wavelength or the $20\text{ cm}$ gap width, so the amount of spreading is unchanged.

B.explanation: Lower frequency gives longer wavelength at constant wave speed, so $\lambda$ becomes closer to the gap width and diffraction increases.

C.explanation: Larger amplitude makes the water waves carry more energy but does not change $\lambda$ relative to gap width, so spreading is unchanged.

D.explanation: A wider gap makes the gap even larger compared with the $5.0\text{ cm}$ wavelength, so the waves spread out less.
